speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you've noticed these skin lesions and have they changed in size, color, or shape over time? Also, are you experiencing any pain, itching, or bleeding associated with them?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the non-healing nature of these lesions and your smoking history, do you recall any history of genital herpes or human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, and have you noticed any swollen lymph nodes in your groin or armpit?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall any history of genital herpes or HPV infection, and have you noticed any swollen lymph nodes in your groin or armpit? Also, have you engaged in unprotected sexual contact recently, and does the lesion on your finger have any history of trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No known malignancies or hereditary diseases in the family. Previous treatments for syphilis and eczema. Social history: Lives with his 4th wife, smokes 2 packs of cigarettes per day for the last 30 years, has recently immigrated from Africa.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Skin Biopsy of penile and finger lesions.

REQUEST TEST: HPV DNA testing and Serology for Syphilis and HIV.

REQUEST IMAGES.

Given the non-healing, crusty nature of these lesions in a heavy smoker with a history of failed syphilis treatment, I must rule out Squamous Cell Carcinoma, particularly the rare extragenital manifestation on the finger which may suggest a viral etiology like HPV.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F), Blood Pressure 130/85 mmHg, Heart Rate 82 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Dermatological Examination: Erythematous plaque with crusting, oozing, and irregular borders on dorsal penile shaft and left middle finger; lesions are firm, non-tender, no warmth; no palpable lymphadenopathy. Biopsy Findings: Cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within follicle-bearing epithelium. STD Panel: Syphilis Negative, HIV Negative, HBV Negative, HCV Negative.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy findings of nuclear hyperchromasia and increased mitotic figures strongly suggest Squamous Cell Carcinoma, likely driven by HPV given the finger involvement. Do you have any known risk factors for HPV infection, such as multiple sexual partners or a lack of circumcision, and have you noticed any new lesions elsewhere on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any systemic symptoms such as fever, weight loss, night sweats, or malaise. No other similar lesions elsewhere on the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy confirms Squamous Cell Carcinoma, and the presence of a lesion on your finger alongside the penile one suggests a specific viral association. Given your recent immigration from Africa, have you ever been diagnosed with a condition called Molluscum contagiosum, or is there any history of chronic skin inflammation or scarring at these sites prior to the lesions appearing?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the penis with rare metastatic or direct inoculation to the finger, likely associated with high-risk HPV infection.
